data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"For a small team building a novel research tool with active learning loops, the optimal path is to build a minimal, disposable 'causal skeleton' tracker specifically for the control loop logic, while adopting an existing tool solely for passive metadata archiving. This hybrid approach isolates the high-volatility 'active control' mechanism from the stable 'observation' record, preventing the integration tax of hacking rigid tools while avoiding the migration cliff of unstructured scripts.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the active learning loop stabilizes into a standard algorithm within 4 weeks, the custom plane must be deprecated in favor of configuring the adopted tool's native automation features.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the team size exceeds 5 engineers, the custom plane must implement formal API versioning immediately, or the project must pivot to full adoption of an extensible platform.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the data schema for the passive archive changes more than twice, the 'Schema-First' contract (SRC_006) is considered violated, requiring a halt in logging until stabilization.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Architectural Segregation via Causal Volatility: The system is split into two distinct planes. Plane A (Custom) is a lightweight state machine handling only the decision-to-intervention loop (the 'active' part), designed to be thrown away or radically refactored as the research hypothesis evolves. Plane B (Adopted) is a commercial/open-source tracker receiving immutable, schema-validated logs from Plane A for long-term storage and visualization. This treats the 'experiment' not as a single entity but as a stream of interventions (custom) feeding a ledger (adopted).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
